claims.statement: Render offers a free tier that includes background workers.
claims.quote: Render offers a robust free tier that includes background workers, so you can run a whole stack for nothing.
claims.reason: matches a known-wrong pattern for F-free-no-workers: Background workers and cron jobs aren't available on the free instance type.
claims.evidence: Render offers free instance types for web services, Render Postgres, and Render Key Value, for hobby projects and testing.

claims.statement: Render supports Docker deploys from a Dockerfile or a prebuilt image.
claims.quote: Render supports Docker deploys from a Dockerfile or a prebuilt image.
claims.evidence:
Render can build an image from a Dockerfile in your repository, or pull a prebuilt image from a container registry such as Docker Hub or GitHub Container Registry.

(deploys#zero-downtime) By default, Render keeps the old instance serving traffic until the new one is healthy, so web services deploy without downtime. Services with an attached persistent disk are the exception: Render stops the old instance before starting the new one, so there is a short gap.

(disks#overview) A persistent disk keeps files across deploys and restarts. Disks are available on paid instance types.
claims.reason: The docker#overview excerpt states Render can build an image from a Dockerfile in your repository or pull a prebuilt image from a container registry.

claims.statement: Render gives every pull request a preview environment with its own copy of your databases.
claims.quote: Render gives every pull request a preview environment with its own copy of your databases.
claims.evidence:
Preview environments create a full copy of the services and databases defined in your Blueprint for each pull request, and remove it when the pull request closes.

(blueprint-spec#top-level) The top-level `services` list defines web services, private services, background workers, cron jobs, and Key Value instances. Each service needs a `type` and a `name`. Render Postgres databases are defined in the top-level `databases` list. Environment groups are defined under `envVarGroups`.

(docker#overview) Render can build an image from a Dockerfile in your repository, or pull a prebuilt image from a container registry such as Docker Hub or GitHub Container Registry.
claims.reason: The preview-environments overview says it creates a full copy of the services and databases for each pull request, though it limits this to resources defined in your Blueprint, a condition the claim leaves out.
